note:
Class 6B, week of 16 November. Notes for myself.

Aarav Sharma has missed four days this month. His mother Sunita told me on the phone (98765 43210) that his father lost his job at the mill and the family cannot pay for anything extra this term; Aarav now helps at the family tea stall before school. He is bright in maths but has not handed in homework for two weeks.

Meenal reads well aloud but freezes in written tests. She needs extra writing practice, and the remedial writing club meets after the last bell. She told me she has epilepsy and is afraid of having a seizure in the exam hall. Her roll no. 6B/23. She walks six kilometres home to Rampur Kalan and has to leave school at the last bell to reach home before dark.

Kabir and Ishaan fight most days during group work. Kabir's parents are separating and he is staying with his grandmother. Ishaan finishes early and gets bored.

Tanvi is far ahead in reading. She could help others, but she is shy. Her family does not have a smartphone or an internet connection. She takes the 3:40 local bus home right after the last period because her mother cooks in two homes until evening.

Lesson
Class: Class 6
Subject: English
Topic: Writing a short description of a place
Length: 40 minutes

draft.title: Class 6 English — Writing a short description of a place

items.heading: Starter (5 minutes)
items.text: The teacher asks the class to name different places in their town and writes ideas on the board. The pupils call out names of local places like parks and markets. The materials needed are the blackboard and chalk.

items.heading: Teach (10 minutes)
items.text: The teacher explains how to write a short description using sensory words for sights and sounds. The pupils listen and note down helpful adjectives on their paper. The materials needed are notebooks and pens.

items.heading: Practise (15 minutes)
items.text: The teacher guides the class to write a four-sentence paragraph describing a familiar local place. The pupils write their paragraphs individually in their notebooks. The materials needed are notebooks and pens.

items.heading: Check (10 minutes)
items.text: The teacher invites pupils to read out their descriptions and provides feedback to the class. The pupils read their sentences aloud and check their own work. The materials needed are the written paragraphs.

items.heading: Homework (0 minutes)
items.text: The teacher assigns the task to write three sentences describing a room in their home. The pupils note down the homework task in their notebooks. The materials needed are notebooks.
